content.title: When is Artemis II launch time? Can you watch launch at Jersey Shore?
content.text: April 1, 2026, 3:46 p.m. ETNASA's Artemis II launch countdown is on as the Artemis II crew gets ready to launch from Florida's Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral as soon as 6:24 p.m. ET tonight in a historic rocket launch that has an eastern launch path that could be visible in New Jersey, particularly along the Jersey Shore.The astronauts on Artemis 2 — NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Christina Koch and Victor Glover and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen — won't land on the moon but will be the first humans to launch toward the moon since the Apollo 17 mission in 1972, more than 50 years ago.When will Artemis II get to the moon, and when will Artemis II return to Earth? The crew will spend their first 24 hours in space, take a four-day journey toward the moon, and then take another four days to return for splashdown on April 10 on Earth.Prepping for their flight around the moon, the Artemis crew boarded the Orion spacecraft at 2:30 p.m. today, which is perched atop NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket. To watch the latest Artemis II launch updates or check out the Artemis II livestream, head to NASA's YouTube page. Artemis II launch live updates can be found on USA TODAY's Florida Today Space Team.NASA has a two-hour window to attempt Artemis II liftoff, meaning that if weather permits, launch can be as late as 8:24 p.m. ET. President Donald Trump, who is set to address the nation tonight on the Iran war, said he'll monitor the planned launch of Artemis II from the White House.On Truth Social, Trump lauded the Artemis II launch, writing, "We are WINNING, in Space, on Earth, and everywhere in between — Economically, Militarily, and now, BEYOND THE STARS. Nobody comes close! America doesn’t just compete, we DOMINATE, and the whole World is watching."The rocket launch today will tee up an upcoming Artemis III (Artemis 3) test flight in 2027, Artemis IV landing in 2028 and NASA's plan to set up a lunar base. If all goes as plan, the crew will get a remarkable view from the far side of the moon and set a record for the farthest distance from Earth at 252,000 miles, surpassing the record set by Apollo 13.With the Florida weather forecast looking good for the space launch — NASA has strict weather guidelines to launch the SLS and Orion spacecraft — is it possible to see the rocket launch near me? Here's details on how to watch the Artemis II launch, time, livestream, rocket path and visibility map, moon mission details and more.Artemis II launch countdown; What time does Artemis 2 launch?The NASA Artemis II rocket launch is as early as 6:24 p.m. ET today, April 1, from Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, Florida. Four Artemis II astronauts will embark on a 10-day mission around the moon — Artemis won't land on the moon — in a NASA-owned SLS rocket, testing the Orion spacecraft's life support systems for the first time with humans.If liftoff today goes as planned, the space mission could set the record for the farthest distance ever traveled from Earth, at 252,000 miles, surpassing the Apollo 13 mission.The 2-hour window for Artemis II launch time today, April 1, opens at 6:24 p.m. ET, meaning if the weather forecast is favorable, Artemis 2 liftoff could happen anytime between 6:24 p.m. ET to 8:24 p.m. ET. Artemis II launch live updates can be found on the NASA website here, with Florida Today, part of the USA TODAY Network, providing Artemis II live coverage.Where to watch Artemis 2 launch; Artemis II launch livestreamTo watch Artemis II launch today, you can head to the NASA YouTube page to catch the Artemis II livestream, or watch the rocket launch on NASA+ on your computer desktop, from the NASA website, or download NASA+ app on you iPhone or Samsung phone.Local TV channels CBS, ABC, NBC, and Fox News will broadcast the launch 2026. Have Amazon Prime Video or Peacock? You can also stream the rocket launch today on Prime, either through your TV or on your phone.The NASA live stream has been active since 7:45 a.m. ET today, with the latest mission updates showing Artemis II fueling underway as of 10 a.m. ET ahead of launch this evening.Watch Artemis II launch on Amazon Prime VideoArtemis II flight path, visibility map; can I see rocket launch near me?While the Artemis II visibility map shows Florida and Georgia with the best views, it's possible you could see the Artemis II rocket launch from New Jersey and along the Jersey Shore. The Artemis II flight path is east, meaning if weather is ideal, people living in parts of NJ, Pennsylvania, Virginia, Maryland, Ohio, West Virginia, Delaware, Washington DC and along the Mid-Atlantic states could spot it in the sky.The SpaceX Atlas V rocket — which lifted off from Cape Canaveral in Florida on March 1 — was spotted as far as North Jersey, and other NASA space launches have been seen from DC to NJ in years past. Keep an eye to the sky!How long will it take Artemis II to get to the moon? When does Artemis II return to Earth?The Artemis II crew will spend about their first 24 hours in orbit to ensure the spacecraft is operating as planned. Then, the crew will take a four-day journey to the moon using an engine firing called "trans-lunar injection," or TLI, blasting them onto a path toward the lunar surface.After a roughly four-day journey near the far side of the moon, the crew heads back to Earth, which takes roughly four days. About 9 ½ days later, Artemis II will return to Earth.Where is Artemis II launching from?Artemis II is launching from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida, from Pad 39B, which has supported some 60 launches over time, including the Apollo 10 mission in 1969. Sadly, it was also the launch pad for Challenger's final flight in 1986, which ended in disaster.Where is Artemis II going? Will Artemis II land on the moon?No, Artemis II will not land on the moon, but the four Artemis II astronauts will fly around the moon for about 10 days. The mission is to test systems and equipment, laying the groundwork for future missions to land on the moon.Is Artemis 2 launch on schedule? NASA live streamYes, Artemis II launch is on schedule as of 3 p.m. ET today, April 1, with the four astronauts in the Orion capsule and preparing to launch as soon as 6:24 p.m. ET, per the NASA live stream. All preparations have gone smoothly, NASA officials said this afternoon.According to NASA, the crew woke up at 9:25 a.m. ET today, had a meal, attended a weather briefing, suited up in their orange Orion Crew Survival System suits. astronauts from a distance today — the crew had to avoid germs — and headed up to the Orion capsule early afternoon. The last people to see the astronauts? A five-person crew known as the "closeout crew," will perform leak checks on Orion's hatches before launch.Lori Comstock is a New Jersey-based news reporter covering trending news with USA TODAY Network's Mid-Atlantic Connect Team. She covers health and other news in the Northeast, including New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Washington DC, Maryland, and Virginia. Reach her at LComstock@usatodayco.com.
